name: Plausible Analytics
summary: Plausible's public docs describe no OAuth flow for third-party apps, so there is no OAuth app to register and no app review to pass. The working path is a per-team Stats API key, which each customer must create in a Business-plan team and paste in, so plan access and per-customer key handling decide whether this works.

verdict.label: Gated
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: About 15 to 30 minutes of your time to create a key on a Business-plan team and call the API (estimate, not from a source).
verdict.timeToProduction: No provider approval step exists. Any customer can connect once their own team on a Business plan creates a key, so the real wait is your build time plus each customer's setup.
verdict.approvalWait: Provider-side: none, because there is no OAuth app to approve. The official pages describe only API keys. Reported: an OAuth request was open on the community board in 2020 and the maintainers answered in 2021 that they had no plans for it; an unmerged pull request from September 2026 wires an OAuth authorize route behind a feature flag, and its status is not confirmed.
verdict.handsOnEffort: Roughly one to two days for a developer to build a key-entry flow, validate keys, and handle per-team scoping and rate limits (estimate).

decideFirst.question: Can your customers connect without ever handling a Plausible key?
decideFirst.guidance: Not with Plausible today as far as the public docs show. The only documented authentication is a Stats API key sent as a Bearer token. A hosted proxy that holds one shared key for all users would avoid per-customer keys, but it gives every user the same access and is a security tradeoff you must accept deliberately.

evidence.note: Both official pages were fetched; neither describes OAuth for third parties. Community MCP projects say the same (s3, s7).

decideFirst.question: Will each customer have its own Plausible team, and does the key owner have the right role?
decideFirst.guidance: Keys are scoped to one team and only see that team's sites. Viewers cannot create keys, and guest viewers or editors for a single site cannot create keys that reach a client's sites. Each customer therefore needs its own team key created by an Owner, Admin, Editor, or Billing member.

evidence.note: Read from the official Stats API reference, including the role table.

decideFirst.question: Do you need write access (creating or changing sites) or read-only stats?
decideFirst.guidance: A Stats API key can run stats queries and read the sites list. Creating, changing, or deleting sites needs a separate Sites API key. Ask for read-only stats unless you truly need site management, since it keeps the key's blast radius small.

evidence.note: Official Stats API reference, authentication section.

phases.name: 1 · Confirm the access model
phases.goal: Establish that no OAuth app exists and choose the key-based path or stop.
phases.duration: Half a day of your time.

steps.title: Check the plan that includes the Stats API
steps.detail: Confirm that your team (and each customer's team) is on a plan that includes the Stats API. The official reference marks it as a Business plan feature.

evidence.note: Official Stats API reference states it is a Business plan feature.

steps.title: Confirm there is no OAuth app registration
steps.detail: Read the official data-access page and the Stats API authentication section. Neither describes a developer console, client ID, client secret, or consent flow for third-party apps. Treat the absence as the decision basis unless Plausible publishes otherwise.

evidence.note: Verified by reading the fetched pages; this is an absence finding, not a provider statement that OAuth will never exist.

steps.title: Check whether an OAuth route has shipped
steps.detail: Look at the open pull request that wires up an OAuth authorize endpoint. It needs a feature flag on the user and its merge status was not confirmed in this research. Re-check before you commit to the key-based design.

evidence.note: Unmerged work in the provider's repository; it is not documentation and may change or be abandoned.

phases.name: 2 · Connect your own team
phases.goal: Create one key on your own team and prove it can query a site.

steps.title: Create a Stats API key
steps.detail: Select the team in the top-right menu, open your account settings, go to API Keys, click New API Key, choose Stats API, and confirm with Create API Key. The key is shown only once, so save it at that moment.

evidence.note: Steps verified on the official page; the settings URL is taken from a secondary guide that describes the same path.

steps.title: Store the key as a secret
steps.detail: Put the key in your secrets manager or environment store, never in source code or logs. Plausible does not let you read it again after creation.

evidence.note: The official page says the key is shown once.

steps.title: Write and test the connector
steps.detail: Send the key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header to the Stats API query endpoint, using the official curl example with your own site ID. Confirm a 200 response with metrics before building anything else.

evidence.note: Example request from the official reference.

phases.name: 3 · Let customers connect
phases.goal: Each customer supplies a key from its own team and the connector validates it on entry.
phases.duration: Minutes per customer once they have a Business team, plus your build time.

steps.title: Give customers setup instructions
steps.detail: Tell each customer to log in, select the team that owns its sites, and have an Owner, Admin, Editor, or Billing member create a Stats API key there. A Viewer cannot do this, and a key from a personal team cannot read a client's team sites.

evidence.note: Official role and team-scoping rules.

steps.title: Validate the key when it is entered
steps.detail: On save, make one cheap authenticated call, such as listing the team's sites, and reject the key with a clear message if the call fails. Store the key against the customer's account record, not a global setting.

evidence.note: The official page says a Stats API key can list sites owned by its team; the validation design is the agent's own recommendation.

steps.title: Budget for the rate limit
steps.detail: The default is 600 requests per hour per Stats API key. Cache results and batch queries, and ask Plausible for more capacity through its contact page if a customer needs it.

evidence.note: Official default rate limit.

phases.name: 4 · Watch for OAuth
phases.goal: Move to OAuth only if Plausible publishes it for third-party apps.

steps.title: Wait for an official OAuth announcement
steps.detail: Nothing in the official pages sets a date for OAuth. Until Plausible documents a registration process, keep the key-based design.

evidence.note: Community and feedback-board history only; the most recent statement found was a 2021 reply saying there were no plans, and a later feedback-board note is about SSO on Enterprise plans, not API OAuth.

scopeTiers.examples: Querying stats, reading the team's sites list
scopeTiers.consequence: Read-only analytics access for the team it was created in; no site creation or changes.

evidence.note: Official reference.

scopeTiers.consequence: Needed only for site management; a separate key type from the Stats API key.

evidence.note: Official reference states creating, changing, or deleting sites needs a Sites API key.

blockers.symptom: A Viewer cannot find or use the New API Key option for the team
blockers.cause: Viewers are not allowed to create keys for a team.
blockers.fix: Ask an Owner, Admin, Editor, or Billing member to create the key.

evidence.note: Official role table; the symptom wording is an inference.

blockers.symptom: A key returns no data for a client's site
blockers.cause: The key was created on a team that does not own the site, or by a guest viewer or editor for that one site.
blockers.fix: Have the client's own team create the key and use that key for the connection.

evidence.note: Official statement that keys cannot query sites owned by another team or sites where the owner is only a guest.

blockers.symptom: The key is missing after you closed the dialog
blockers.cause: Plausible shows the key only once at creation.
blockers.fix: Create a new key and store it immediately; do not rely on viewing it later.

evidence.note: Official instruction to save the key because it is shown once.

blockers.symptom: Requests fail after a burst of traffic
blockers.cause: The default limit of 600 requests per hour per Stats API key is exceeded.
blockers.fix: Cache and batch queries, or request more capacity from Plausible.

evidence.note: Official rate limit; the failure symptom is an inference, and the HTTP status code was not confirmed.

nuances.title: Keys belong to a team, not to a user
nuances.detail: A key is tied to the team selected when it is created. It does not inherit access to every site its owner can see, so the same person may need different keys for different teams.

evidence.note: Official statement.

nuances.title: No OAuth token lifetime or refresh behavior to design around
nuances.detail: Because the public pages describe only static keys, there is no access-token expiry or refresh-token flow in the documented model. The official pages read here do not state whether keys expire or can be rotated; check the account UI before you rely on rotation.

evidence.note: Absence on the official page; expiry and rotation were not stated either way.

nuances.title: Community tooling confirms the gap
nuances.detail: Community MCP servers say Plausible has no OAuth sign-in and require a key or a shared server-side key. One community server's OAuth 2.1 support is listed as not implemented.

evidence.note: Secondary sources; they support the finding but are not official.

nuances.title: Single sign-on is a different feature
nuances.detail: Plausible's SSO is for logging into the Plausible dashboard and is available on Enterprise plans. It is not an OAuth connection for third-party apps.

evidence.note: Stated on Plausible's feedback board in a search excerpt; not checked on a docs page.
